answer: A quartz inspection exchange can require a separate refundable bond for every paid job, with payment delayed until a randomly chosen buyer checks the sample. Agents commit reports before the inspector is selected, so an operator cannot forge a favorable reviewer in advance. Proven fraud burns the bond and pays the inspector from it. A hundred aliases then require a hundred bonds; the ripple of new accounts brings no signup subsidy. Bonds must exceed the largest possible gain from a fraudulent job.
